source_title: Dragon Ball Super Chapter 105: Toyotarou Teases Black Frieza Saga
source_excerpt:

Where Dragon Ball Super Chapter 104 left off, the manga had flashed back in time to a prequel chapter setting up the High School Saga starring Trunks and Goten. Even though the chapter was released after Akira Toriyama's death, it was based on dialogue, story, and an outline provided by him that simply went unused during Toyotarou's adaptation of Dragon Ball Super: Super Hero . The manga has been on hiatus ever since, but Toyotarou has finally dropped a new hint at the Black Frieza Saga.
After years of silence, Toyotarou is getting fans ready for the release of Dragon Ball Super Chapter 105 by teasing the Black Frieza Saga on X. Each month, the Dragon Ball Super mangaka draws a new character, form, or design tied to something that is happening in the larger franchise. With Dragon Ball Super: Beerus in the midst of airing, the fact that Toyotarou is reminding everyone of the danger of Black Frieza feels significant.
Toyotarou Drops Another Teaser For The Dragon Ball Super Manga's Final Arc
The way Toyotarou's promo art has historically worked, the Dragon Ball Super mangaka is always subtly dropping hints and teasers at the next story arcs to come. In recent months, he dropped a new redesign of Super Saiyan Hercule to set up Dragon Ball Super: Beerus , as well as art of minor villains from the Moro arc as marketing for Dragon Ball Super: The Galactic Patrol . Every now and then, however, Toyotarou will unveil a new artwork that has no obvious ties to the story... yet.
Several recent pieces of art from Toyotarou are clearly being used to set up the Black Frieza Saga. There is no reason Dragon Ball Super Volume 24 would feature key art of Perfected Ultra Instinct Goku, Ultra Ego Vegeta, Gohan Beast, Orange Piccolo, and True Legendary Super Saiyan Broly on the front cover otherwise (especially since Ultra Ego Vegeta never appears in the volume). This goes double for Black Frieza, who appears on the back cover despite not being seen since the start of the Super Hero Saga.
Throw in Toyotarou's Elderly Goku redesign from a few months ago and the bizarre decision to draw Guarana – an obscure manga character who has been suddenly retconned into the Frieza Force's second-most powerful soldier – and it's painfully obvious that everything Toyotarou has done as of late has been for the return of the series (a sentiment he has explicitly shared on his personal Twitter).
Everything We Know About Black Frieza Saga So Far
Despite the secrecy surrounding the upcoming story arc, we actually know quite a few details about the Black Frieza Saga based on publishing leaks and Toyotarou's own hints. Planeta Cómic, a Spanish publisher, accidentally used the wrong spine art for their versions of Dragon Ball Super Volumes 23 and 24, confirming that the series will go up to at least Volume 26 (with the spine art implying there will be even more to come).
The existence of spine art for two unpublished volumes means that Toyotarou has at least eight chapters completed in some fashion for the Black Frieza Saga. Based on the promo art, we know that Frieza will be the main villain, the five main Z-Fighters are the protagonists, and that the Frieza Force will play a major role – especially with someone as minor as Guarana being given the title of being Frieza's "number two powerhouse." With the Black Frieza Saga being so close to the End of Z, there's also a very real chance this will be the Dragon Ball Super manga's last story arc out of respect towards Akira Toriyama.
Masako Nozawa Son Goku/Goku Black/Son Gohan/Son Goten (voices)
